clue.text: Beaver a bit to sort out contract

indicators.note: sorting things out means putting them into a new order, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter as raw material

explanation.surface: A busy rodent spends some time tidying up a legal agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun for a deal, but here it is the verb meaning to shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: To abbreviate a word is to shorten it, which is one sense of the verb contract.

clue.text: Flowers for old tennis champion accepting downfall

indicators.note: one thing accepting another takes it inside itself, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Rod Laver, the Australian who won two calendar Grand Slams in the 1960s
a downfall is the end of someone

explanation.surface: Someone sends a bouquet to a retired tennis star who has fallen from grace.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod Laver is the Australian who won two calendar Grand Slams; the downfall sits inside his name after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender is a fragrant plant whose purple blooms are sold as flowers.

clue.text: Australian woman's quiet about a romance

parts.note: the sound made to ask for quiet

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the words after it are read from back to front

parts.note: to romance is to tell fanciful stories, so a romance here is a lie

explanation.surface: An Australian woman keeps quiet about a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romance' poses as a love affair; as a verb it means to exaggerate or fib, so it stands for a lie here.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheila is Australian slang for a woman or girl.

clue.text: Joke about name of team

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a gag is a joke
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone makes a joke about what a sports team is called.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a group of people working together, much as a team is.

clue.text: Florist's son's getting into River Dance

indicators.note: getting into something means entering it, so one piece is placed inside the rest

parts.note: a crossword joke: a river is something that flows, a flow-er
a hop is an informal dance
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A florist's boy is taking up Riverdance, the Irish stepdance show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River' read as flow-er, something that flows, is a classic crossword trick; the son goes between the river and the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The florist's' is the florist's premises, that is the shop where flowers are sold.

clue.text: Journalist's leader's in the style of writer on love — hot stuff!

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word
the French phrase a la means in the style of
a pen is a writing instrument
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An editor's style piece on love turns out to be steamy stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer on love' puts PEN before O, as in a down clue one sits on the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalapeno is a spicy chilli pepper, literally hot food.

clue.text: Try to perform forfeit without involving me

indicators.note: to perform something is to work it, so the letters are worked into a new order
without involving the speaker means leaving out the first-person letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to pay a penalty without getting the speaker involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Me' stands for I, which is removed from FORFEIT before the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort is an attempt, the noun sense of try.

clue.text: Brexiteer's content to leave

indicators.note: the content of a word is what lies inside it, so the answer sits among its letters

parts.note: letters three to six of the word

explanation.surface: A Brexit supporter is happy for the country to leave the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like the adjective happy, but it is the noun meaning what is inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to go out or depart, a plain synonym of leave.

clue.text: Seaside entertainer's top banana at every party!

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across clue is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
each and every are synonyms
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: A comedian at the beach is the top banana, star of every party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top banana' reads as a slang phrase for the main person, but top only picks the first letter of banana.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable ball bounced about on the sand amuses beachgoers, so it is playfully called an entertainer.

clue.text: Join fellows following a team's comeback

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the fellows are placed second, after the single letter

parts.note: taken as written
F is fellow, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the word for the side is read backwards

parts.note: a cricket or football team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: New players sign up after a club stages a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the fellows after the A; a football or cricket side has eleven players, written as the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To affix is to attach or fasten one thing onto another.

clue.text: Humming is about to finally irritate man

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the closing letter of the word
a king is a man, as in a chess piece

explanation.surface: Someone humming a tune is about to annoy a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humming' looks like making a tuneful noise, but it is British slang for smelling bad.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal use, something humming gives off a strong smell, which is what reeking means.

clue.text: Exhaust us with one big defeat

parts.note: we is the subject form of us
a means one
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: A heavy loss leaves the whole team worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear someone out is to tire them completely, the verb sense of exhaust.

clue.text: Dvorak composed with outright spirit

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters are set in a new order
read as out right, it tells the solver to put out the abbreviation for right

parts.note: the Czech composer's name taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Dvorak wrote music full of straightforward spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' looks like a reference to Dvorak writing music. 'Outright' splits as out right: R leaves before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is a clear distilled alcoholic drink, and spirit is the general term for such liquor.

clue.text: Chippy has fish come in

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
to enter is to come in

explanation.surface: A fish and chip shop has fish arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chippy' suggests a British fish and chip shop, which suits the fish, but here it is slang for a woodworker.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a chippy is a joiner or woodworker, from the chips of wood they make.

clue.text: Rent/buy car to get around city

indicators.note: getting around suggests moving about, so the letters move into another arrangement

parts.note: the words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Hire or purchase a car to drive round a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a cathedral city in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Canterbury is a cathedral city in Kent, seat of the Archbishop of Canterbury.

clue.text: Mum has rest disrupted by call from big top manager

parts.note: to ring is to telephone, to call

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother's nap is interrupted by a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled pair comes after the call, as 'by' lets the call stand beside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringmaster runs the show in a circus, whose tent is the big top.

clue.text: Insignificant part of the whole Mariana Trench?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tiny amount compared with what is needed
second meaning, read literally: the deepest dip in the sea floor of the Pacific

explanation.surface: Is the Mariana Trench a minor feature of the seabed?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading: the trench is a plunge in the Pacific seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a contribution too small to matter; literally the trench is a great fall in sea depth.

clue.text: Take advantage of working to support production at university

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits underneath, so it comes after the rest

parts.note: a play is a stage production
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford
on means operating or working

explanation.surface: Someone works backstage on a student production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At university' is up because British students go up to university, as in up at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: To play upon someone's fears is to exploit them, which is to take advantage of them.

clue.text: Sleep in the Spanish quarter, after eating first with Doctor Nick

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

indicators.note: in places the sleep inside the other letters

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
zz is the cartoon sound of snoring
E for east, a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone takes a siesta in the Spanish quarter after eating with Doctor Nick.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish and the quarter combine as ELE, with the sleep inside after its first letter. 'Nick' looks like a name; it is British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To embezzle is to steal money entrusted to you, and nick is British slang for steal.

clue.text: Look at ingredients of face paint?

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
the make-up of something is what it is composed of

explanation.surface: A cosmetics fan reads the ingredients list on some face paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye make-up, such as mascara and eyeshadow, is cosmetics applied to the face.

clue.text: See about set-up of ISA with no trouble

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: a set-up is an arrangement, so these letters are arranged differently

parts.note: an ISA is a British tax-free savings account

explanation.surface: Someone checks how a tax-free savings account was opened without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, but it is a bishop's diocese, a favourite crossword source for ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something easily means doing it without difficulty or effort.

clue.text: LP for a pound? Not sure about that!

parts.note: taken as written
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
um is the sound of hesitation or doubt

explanation.surface: Someone is offered a record for a pound and has doubts about the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An LP, a long-playing record, is a full-length music album.

clue.text: Moon mission gets ahead with initial orbit

parts.note: read as a head; poll is an old word for the head, as in a poll tax

indicators.note: initial means the opening one, so just the first letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A lunar mission takes the lead by first going into orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead' splits as a head, giving A POLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo was the NASA programme whose missions landed astronauts on the Moon.

clue.text: Upset by rejection of offer to contain rust problem

indicators.note: rejection here means sending back, so the word for offer is read backwards
to contain is to hold inside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a bid is an offer

indicators.note: a problem suggests something gone wrong, so the letters before it are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is upset when their offer to fix a rust problem is turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb someone is to trouble or agitate them, the verb sense of upset.

clue.text: Pack ornament

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a set of playing cards
second meaning: to adorn or decorate

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns; the second is a verb meaning to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: A deck is a full set of playing cards, and to deck something is to decorate it.

clue.text: Southern ozone's dispersion is dropping off

indicators.note: dispersion is a scattering, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
taken letter for letter, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: The ozone layer in the southern hemisphere is thinning out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping off' looks like declining ozone, but it means falling asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who snoozes is falling into a light sleep, which is what dropping off means.

clue.text: Scottish island's engulfed by the "Whisky Experience"

indicators.note: being engulfed by words means sitting inside them, so the answer lies within the letters that follow

parts.note: the last three letters of the first word and the first of the second

explanation.surface: A Scottish island is overrun by a whisky-tasting tourist attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides, off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Little room has nothing with which to make music

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A tiny room has nothing in it to play music on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description rather than a synonym: the answer is a thing with which to make music.
explanation.definitionFit: A cello is a large bowed string instrument, so it is something used to play music.

clue.text: Queen dejected in the shade

parts.note: a queen is a royal
feeling blue means feeling sad

explanation.surface: A melancholy queen sits out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' suggests shelter from the sun, but it means a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep bright blue, a particular shade of colour.
